newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks rise 0.77 percent to fresh record.
newsitem.headline: French stocks rise 0.77 percent to fresh record.

text.p: French shares rose 0.77 percent on Thursday to a fresh record close -- the sixth this year -- with financial stocks blazing the trail.
Shares in banks Societe Generale and Credit Commercial de France (CCF) led the rally. Other blue chips in the long-suffering sector advanced, sweeping the CAC index to all-time highs, traders said.
The Paris market was also helped by a buoyant Wall Street and a surge in London equities.
The bourse's blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 18.79 points or 0.77 percent at 2,461.25. It hit an intra-day and historic high of 2,463.91 points.
The CAC-40 futures contract rose 20 points to 2,465.
Volume was a heavy 8.78 billion francs.
Societe Generale shares rose 4.41 percent to 592 francs on bullish forecasts for 1996 profit and second-half capital gains.
Paribas Capital Markets issued a favourable report on Societe Generale, estimating the stock would outperform the rest of the market by 12 percent in the medium term.
Broker Massonaud raised its recommendation on CCF to buy from neutral. CCF ended up 7.6 percent at 254.80 francs.
Other gainers in the sector included bank BNP, up 5.84 percent, insurer Axa, up 1.87 percent, and Compagnie Bancaire, up 3.73 percent.
Shares in French hotel group Accor rose 5.5 percent to 691 francs after long-time seller Paribas Capital Markets upgraded its stock for the second time in as many weeks.

Paribas analyst Nigel Reed rates the stock a buy based on favourable economic indicators and currency shifts. The franc's weakness relative to the dollar is expected to draw tourism to France and will also translate into higher earnings for Accor from its U.S. subsidiary Motel 6.
